mechanism_narrative: A high level of residential construction (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand for housing, which typically precedes positive equity market returns as the economy expands. The signal is active at all times and does not require a threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST is above 550, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative equity returns as economic growth slows. The signal activates when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreases in industrial production (INDPRO) signal monetary tightening and supply contraction, which typically cause negative equity returns due to reduced economic activity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a federal funds rate above 0.1% and rising for three months typically leads to negative equity returns as central bank policy restricts liquidity and growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in residential construction (HOUST) below 550 units signals weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes negative equity market returns as economic activity contracts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 550, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative equity returns due to reduced corporate earnings and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decreases in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal a tightening labor market, which typically drives positive equity returns as employment growth boosts consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of residential construction (HOUST) consistently correlates with positive equity market returns over the medium term, as housing activity is a leading indicator of economic expansion and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST is above 550, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
